messages.author: 28ff89d8ea06c5a9
messages.subject: dyadic growth model
parts:
Hi,

First time posting... I am attempting to run a dyadic growth model in lavaan using the following syntax.

m1 <- 'ip1 =~ 1*PSS.1.00 + 1*PSS_W2.1.00 + 1*PSS_W3.1.00
           sp1 =~ 0*PSS.1.00 + 1*PSS_W2.1.00 + 2*PSS_W3.1.00
           ip2 =~ 1*PSS.2.00 + 1*PSS_W2.2.00 + 1*PSS_W3.2.00
           sp2 =~ 0*PSS.2.00 + 1*PSS_W2.2.00 + 2*PSS_W3.2.00
                
         '
fit_m1 <- growth(m1, missing="ML", data=MERGED4)
modindices(fit_m1, sort = TRUE, maximum.number = 5)
summary(fit_m1, fit.measures=TRUE, standardized=TRUE)

This model runs fine, but in the reference below, I am told to implement a number of constraints on the latent intercepts and slopes. I have no idea how to do so. For reference, ip1 = intercept person 1, and sp1 = slope person 1, etc.

My dyads are indistinguishable, hence the need for the constraints. Any help would be greatly appreciated. And, if anyone has worksheets, calculators, etc. for adjusting fit indices I would be interested in that as well.

Reference:
Iida, M., Savord, A., & Ledermann, T. (2023). Dyadic longitudinal models: A critical review. Personal Relationships, 30(2), 356–378. https://doi.org/10.1111/pere.12468

Many thanks!
Loren

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: dyadic growth model
parts: I am told to implement a number of constraints on the latent intercepts and slopes. I have no idea how to do so. For reference, ip1 = intercept person 1, and sp1 = slope person 1, etc.

You can see how to specify variance and intercept parameters here: https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/syntax1.html
You can see how to place equality constraints by using the same label here: https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/syntax2.html#simple-equality-constraints

Don't forget to specify the "inter-person residual correlations" mentioned in Section 4.2
if anyone has worksheets, calculators, etc. for adjusting fit indices I would be interested in that as well.

Adjusting fit indices?  If you mean that you need to specify equal intercepts and variances across partners in the independence model (to calculate the correct CFI, TLI, etc.), then you can just fit that constrained independence model yourself and pass it to the fitMeasures(..., baseline.model=) argument.

parts:
Hi Terrence,

Thanks so much for your reply. My model is a growth model, so I need to set constraints on the latent intercept and variance because of the dyadic nature of the data.  Text is below:

If a researcher has an indistinguishable dyadic design, they will need to apply a set of constraints and adjust the fit of the model (Kashy et al., 2008; Olsen & Kenny, 2006).

The first set of constraints is that the two means of the latent intercepts and the two means of the latent slopes need to be set equal. (both are latent)

Another set of constraints is that the variances of the intercepts, the slopes (both are latent), and the residuals (of the observed variables) need to be set equal across the two dyad members. 

A final set of constraints is that the intra-person and inter-person associations between the intercept and slope factors are set
equal for both partners. (these are estimated automatically by lavaan, so I don't know how to constrain them).

I'm still quite new to R, but I think the "growth" script is designed to help estimate growth models easily, but then makes it difficult to make adjustments when the dyadic growth model is employed. The links you shared are helpful, but I don't know how to employ these constraints when the elements that need constraining are latent or "implicit" in the model syntax.

Truly appreciate your help!

Loren

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: dyadic growth model
parts: My model is a growth model, so I need to set constraints on the latent intercept and variance because of the dyadic nature of the data.
The latent intercept and latent slope are variables.  Each of them has an intercept and a variance.  Follow the links to see how to specify them.
The first set of constraints is that the two means of the latent intercepts and the two means of the latent slopes need to be set equal. (both are latent)

For example:

ip1 ~ mean_int*1
ip2 ~ mean_int*1
Another set of constraints is that the variances of the intercepts, the slopes (both are latent), and the residuals (of the observed variables) need to be set equal across the two dyad members.

For example:

ip1 ~~ var_int*ip1
ip2 ~~ var_int*ip2

A final set of constraints is that the intra-person and inter-person associations between the intercept and slope factors are set
equal for both partners. (these are estimated automatically by lavaan, so I don't know how to constrain them).

You just have to specify them in your syntax.

## intraperson
ip1 ~~ i_s_Cov_intra*sp1
ip2 ~~ i_s_Cov_intra*sp2
## interperson
ip1 ~~ i_s_Cov_inter*sp2
ip2 ~~ i_s_Cov_inter*sp1

Also estimate interpersonal correlations of indicators:

PSS.1.00 ~~ PSS.2.00

And set the residual variances equal across partners:

PSS.1.00 ~~ evar1*PSS.1.00
PSS.2.00 ~~ evar1*PSS.2.00
I'm still quite new to R, but I think the "growth" script is designed to help estimate growth models easily
Only simple growth models.
but then makes it difficult to make adjustments when the dyadic growth model is employed
For anything more complex, just specify your model parameters in the syntax and use the lavaan() function instead of a shortcut that doesn't work for your situation.
